patient_overview.name: Dia Kovacek
patient_overview.description: Dia Kovacek is a 36-year-old White woman from Irvington, New Jersey, who just finished a difficult pregnancy and a tubal ligation and is now navigating chronic neck pain, long-standing sepsis history, and a BMI that has crossed into the obesity range. She comes across as bright and well-read about nutrition — she can quote macros and inflammation theories from Instagram reels — but she is scattered in conversation, often answering a question with another question and losing track of what she was explaining. Underneath the information overload, she seems stretched thin, though she keeps steering the conversation away from herself. A dietetics student will need patience and gentle redirection to keep the visit on track.

demographics.occupation: Not currently in the labor force; previously worked part-time as a receptionist at a dental office before her youngest was born
demographics.cultural_context: Dia grew up in a working-class household in northern New Jersey where meals were whatever was quick and filling between shifts; nobody sat down to teach her to cook, so as an adult she has pieced together her food knowledge from the internet rather than family tradition. She takes pride in being the one who 'actually researches stuff' for her household, even though she sometimes feels embarrassed that she never went to college and worries people won't take her seriously when she brings up something she read.

current_symptoms: Constant dull ache across the neck and shoulders that flares by late afternoon
Generalized fatigue that she attributes to 'just being a mom of four now'
Occasional dizziness when she stands up too fast
Trouble falling asleep because her mind races through the next day's errands
Low-grade headaches a few times a week
clinical_findings: Appears tired, with dark circles under her eyes and slightly disheveled hair pulled back in a hurry
Mild forward-head posture and reduced neck rotation, rubbing the back of her neck repeatedly during conversation
Carries extra weight around the midsection, abdomen soft and non-tender on observation
Speech is quick and jumps between topics, occasionally stopping mid-sentence to ask the interviewer a question instead of finishing her own thought

medications.name: Acetaminophen 325 MG Oral Tablet [Tylenol]
medications.frequency: Takes as needed, roughly 2-3 times a week
medications.adherence: Inconsistent; forgets it in her bag half the time or takes it late when the neck pain is already bad
medications.patient_concerns: Worries she's 'relying on pills too much' but isn't sure what else to do for the pain, and read online that Tylenol can be hard on the liver if you take too much

supplements_and_otc: Magnesium glycinate (started after a TikTok video about 'moms and stress')
Elderberry gummies for immune support, taken on and off
A collagen powder a friend recommended for joint pain that she sometimes stirs into coffee

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Currently attempting a modified 'anti-inflammatory' eating plan she found through a wellness influencer and a friend from her mom's group, cutting out gluten and most dairy but not consistently
food_preferences: Smoothies with frozen berries and spinach when she has time to blend them
Rotisserie chicken from the ShopRite on Springfield Ave because it's fast and feels 'less processed'
Rice cakes with almond butter as a go-to snack
Avoids bread and pasta most days but will eat them when she's too exhausted to cook anything else
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Skipping meals entirely on days when childcare and errands take over
Reliance on gas-station snacks when she's out running kids to appointments and has no time to eat
Possible under-eating overall despite the 'clean eating' intent, given her fatigue and weight pattern
Use of online supplement recommendations without checking for interactions
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Irregular; breakfast is often just coffee, lunch gets skipped or eaten standing at the counter, dinner is whatever can be made in under 20 minutes for the kids and whatever's left for her
nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly water but admits she sometimes goes most of the day without drinking much because she 'forgets' between errands
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: No structured exercise; on her feet a lot chasing kids and doing housework but describes herself as 'too wiped out' for anything intentional
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Light alcohol use, roughly a drink or two on occasion (AUDIT-C score 2); never smoked
nutrition_profile.sleep: Difficulty falling asleep most nights, averaging maybe 5-6 hours, mind racing with to-do lists

psychosocial_profile.personality: Scattered and overwhelmed, talks fast and jumps topics, often answers a question by asking one back as if buying time to think
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Deflects direct questions with questions of her own ('Well, what do you think I should do?'), gives a lot of information but circles back and repeats herself, needs gentle structure to stay on topic
goals: Wants her neck pain to stop interfering with daily tasks
Hopes to lose some weight but mostly wants to 'feel like herself again'
Wants to find an eating plan that actually sticks instead of the next trendy one
concerns: Worried the pain medication isn't 'real medicine' for the pain and she's just masking it
Anxious about her weight gain since the pregnancy
Nervous about her blood test numbers she glimpsed in her patient portal but doesn't fully understand
beliefs: Believes cutting gluten and dairy will fix inflammation and pain
Believes she should be able to figure this out herself since she 'reads so much' about health
Believes doctors are too rushed to really listen, so she researches instead
motivations: Wants to have energy to keep up with her kids
Doesn't want to end up back in the hospital like she did with the sepsis years ago
Wants to feel in control of something in her life right now
fears: Fear of her health declining further while she's busy caring for everyone else
Fear of being judged for her weight or her diet choices
Fear that she's quietly failing at everything, even though she won't say it that plainly
barriers: No real time carved out for her own meals or appointments
Transportation problems that have made her miss things before
Limited budget stretched across a household of five
Mental load of caregiving leaves little bandwidth for consistent self-care
Chronic neck pain limits how much cooking or meal prep she can tolerate standing up
strengths: Genuinely motivated to learn and willing to try new things
Has a strong support person she leans on
Already tracks some of her symptoms and triggers informally
Resourceful at finding information and stretching a tight budget
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Her next-door neighbor and close friend, Renata, is her main support — picks up groceries when transportation falls through, watches the kids in a pinch, and is the person Dia actually talks to about how she's really doing
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Contemplation: aware something needs to shift with her eating and pain management but feels torn between competing responsibilities and unsure where to start

initial_information: States she has chronic neck pain that's been going on since 2014 and some days it's worse than others
Mentions she just had a baby in March and then had her tubes tied in May
Says she's been trying to eat 'anti-inflammatory' because she read it helps with pain and weight
Mentions she takes Tylenol for the neck pain when it gets bad
discoverable_information: Describes her actual daily meal pattern once asked directly, revealing skipped meals and irregular eating
Admits she doesn't always understand the lab numbers she sees in her patient portal and gets anxious about them
Reveals she has transportation problems that have made her miss appointments or grocery trips
Talks about her neighbor Renata helping out with the kids and errands when asked about her support system
Mentions the household income is tight and sometimes food runs short toward the end of the month
reluctant_information: Eventually admits she is the full-time caregiver for her elderly mother-in-law three days a week on top of her own four kids, and that's why she has no time to cook or go to appointments for herself
Admits that she sometimes doesn't eat at all until dinner because she's feeding everyone else first and 'just forgets' herself
hidden_information: Dia has gone an entire day without eating at least twice in the past month while juggling her mother-in-law's care and her kids, something she hasn't told anyone including Renata
She has started skipping her own follow-up calls about her cholesterol results because she 'doesn't have the mental space' to deal with one more thing right now

opportunities.learning_objective: Elicit a complete and honest 24-hour dietary recall despite a scattered communication style
expected_discoveries: Meals are skipped or eaten standing up
Self-directed elimination diet is inconsistently followed
Possible caloric and nutrient inadequacy despite 'clean eating' intent
possible_patient_reactions: 'Wait, are you asking about yesterday or like a normal day? Because yesterday was weird...'
'I mean I eat pretty clean, don't I seem like I eat clean?'
Loses train of thought and needs to be redirected back to the recall

opportunities.learning_objective: Explore the patient's self-directed anti-inflammatory diet and assess evidence versus misinformation
expected_discoveries: Diet was adopted from an influencer and a friend without professional guidance
Patient has some accurate health literacy mixed with myths about gluten and inflammation
Openness to modifying the approach if given credible, concrete alternatives
possible_patient_reactions: 'I read that gluten causes inflammation everywhere, isn't that true?'
Becomes defensive if she feels her research is being dismissed outright
Relieved if the student validates what's useful in her plan while gently correcting myths

opportunities.learning_objective: Uncover hidden caregiving responsibilities that limit time and energy for self-care
expected_discoveries: Dia cares for her mother-in-law three days a week in addition to four children
This caregiving load is the real reason behind skipped meals and missed appointments
She has not disclosed this burden to her medical team before
possible_patient_reactions: Deflects at first with a joke or a question back
'Why do you need to know about that, isn't this supposed to be about my neck?'
Opens up more once she feels the student isn't going to judge or add to her load

opportunities.learning_objective: Assess readiness to change and use motivational interviewing to move her from contemplation toward action
expected_discoveries: Dia knows something needs to change but feels torn between caregiving duties and her own needs
She responds well when her own stated goals are reflected back to her
Small, concrete steps feel more achievable to her than a full plan overhaul
possible_patient_reactions: 'I know I should do something but where would I even start?'
Shows relief when offered one small, specific change rather than a whole new diet
May spiral into listing everything wrong before settling on one manageable goal

opportunities.learning_objective: Identify social and economic barriers, including transportation and food access, affecting nutrition care
expected_discoveries: Transportation problems have caused missed grocery trips and appointments
Household income is tight for a family of five and she reports having gone without food at times
Her neighbor Renata is a key practical support for groceries and childcare
possible_patient_reactions: Mentions Renata helping out, almost in passing, as if it's not a big deal
Hesitant to say she's gone without food, downplays it as 'just a busy week'
Grateful if offered concrete resource information like food assistance programs

assumptions: Assumed her previous work history as a receptionist to fit 'otherwise unemployed, not seeking work' status with a high school education
Assumed the unnamed caregiving duty from the assigned trait is for her mother-in-law, since household size is 5 and children are implied by recent pregnancy
Assumed GAD-7 score of 7 (mild anxiety) manifests as racing thoughts and difficulty sleeping rather than panic symptoms
Assumed 'went without: Food' on the social survey corresponds to intermittent food insecurity rather than chronic severe insecurity
optional_details: Dia keeps a running Notes app list on her phone titled 'things to ask doctor' that she rarely gets through
She has a favorite mug from a work conference years ago that she still drinks her one cup of coffee from each morning
Renata leaves extra produce from her own garden on Dia's porch some weeks in summer
